pullRequests.title: fix(carry): name the release's empty level hooks by their callers
pullRequests.author: nickyyOO
pullRequests.head: fix/hook-names-by-callers
pullRequests.body:
Before: the boot's empty 8-byte level hooks were paired with v1.01's by order. USA v2.00 has its hooks 8 bytes on and one more, and PAL has its own run, so many release hooks had another hook's name (func_0026F748, the hero's state change hook, among them). OpenRAC had to pair them again by their callers (pair_stubs).
After: carry.py pairs each hook by the calls to it. A v1.01 function with a place in the release, or the one release function of the same shape, calls the release's hook at the…

commits.headline: refactor(names): name globals and PAL/USA v2.00 functions, rac1 style
commits.author: Lynder063
commits.body:
- 14,367 globals get g_snake_case names: 14,072 USA v1.01 data symbols and
  295 that only the PAL or USA v2.00 sources use. A name several levels
  share takes _lNN after its first word. 24 compiler jump tables keep their
  address names.
- 2,101 PAL/USA v2.00 functions that are a release's version of a named
  v1.01 function take its name plus _pal or _us2 (build/<version>/carry.json

commits.headline: docs(src): readable PAL and USA v2.00 sources, rac1 style
commits.author: Lynder063
commits.body:
- 2,545 functions only PAL or USA v2.00 has get snake_case names, system
  first; a release's version of a v1.01 function takes its name plus _pal
  or _us2. They go in include/names/pal.h and us2.h.
- Simple English comments above the release functions that had none (about
  4,500 of 4,990 definitions now have one), reusing the v1.01 counterpart's
  comment where it still fits.
- Locals, parameters and in-file struct fields renamed to snake_case;
  260 moby class ids written as MOBY_CLASS_*…
